advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Preserve (or explicitly decide to drop) non-bullet prose inside the SC block when merging into an existing AC block, matching the in-place path's behavior.
evidence: scripts/migrate_success_criteria.py:106: `items = [ln.strip() for ln in sc_checkbox_body.split("\n") if ln.strip().startswith("- [")]`
In-place path preserves prose: `replacement = _AC_HEADING + sc_checkbox_body` (line 101), whereas the merge path only keeps `- [` lines

ABSENCE: heldout test `test_non_bullet_prose_inside_the_block_is_not_checkboxed` (tests/scripts/test_migrate_success_criteria_heldout.py:106) exercises the NO-AC path only; there is no test for SC framing prose when an AC block already exists
ABSENCE: no test covers indented/nested SC bullets on the merge path
advisory.finding: In the merge path (existing AC block present), any non-bullet prose inside the `## Success Criteria` block is silently discarded: only lines matching `- [` are carried over. This is data loss and is asymmetric with the in-place (no-AC) path, which preserves the full SC body.
merged_from: The merge path calls `.strip()` on each carried item, flattening leading indentation. Nested/indented SC sub-bullets (which `_checkbox_body` correctly preserves indentation for) lose their nesting when merged into an existing AC block.
scenarios: A closed ticket with both a `## Acceptance Criteria` block and a `## Success Criteria` block that begins with a framing sentence before its bullets — the sentence is dropped on migration

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip (or flag) SC blocks that yield zero checklist items, since renaming them does not satisfy the check-ac floor.
evidence: scripts/migrate_success_criteria.py:101: `replacement = _AC_HEADING + sc_checkbox_body` — with no bullets, sc_checkbox_body carries no `- [` lines
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:165: `if found and ln.startswith("- ["): count += 1` — zero items counted for a bullet-less block

advisory.finding: An SC block with a heading but no `- ` bullets still produces a description change (renamed to `## Acceptance Criteria`) and is counted as migrated, yet `_count_ac_items` still returns 0 for it, so the migration's stated goal (reach the blocking floor) is not met for such tickets.
scenarios: A ticket whose `## Success Criteria` section contains only prose (no bullets) is reported as migrated but still fails the AC floor

migrate() at scripts/migrate_success_criteria.py:147-163 has `if not write: return 0` and the edit_ticket loop — both branches unexercised
advisory.finding: The write path (`migrate` calling `rebar.edit_ticket`) and its dry-run safety contract are untested despite the held-out file's docstring claiming coverage of 'the write path: `--dry-run` is the default and writes nothing'. No test references `migrate`, `propose_migrations`, or `rebar.edit_ticket`, so a regression that writes during dry-run, fails to write with `--write`, or double-writes would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor makes `migrate` write during dry-run (e.g. dropping the `if not write` guard)
`rebar.edit_ticket` is called with a wrong kwarg name and silently no-ops
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests using a real repo fixture (as in test_backfill_caused_by_heldout.py) or by monkeypatching `rebar.list_tickets`/`rebar.edit_ticket`: one asserting dry-run leaves descriptions untouched (edit_ticket never called), one asserting `--write` invokes edit_ticket once per proposal with the rewritten description.
